page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, achieving an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation, VNNI, and BF16), as well as AES and SHA-NI cryptographic instruction sets.

The virtual machine does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent data. Networking infrastructure provides a baseline bandwidth of 7 Gbps. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not available on this server type.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25 percent for single-threaded stress-ng (3073.58) and Geekbench (1989.0) scores, along with high text processing results. Multi-core performance remains in the middle 50 percent with a stress-ng score of 24599.01 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11631.0. While small-block cached memory bandwidth reaches 1216.0 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to 37.89 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25 percent. In-memory execution throughput is demonstrated by 21.76 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

This hardware profile delivers high memory density relative to core count, making it cost-efficient for workloads bounded by memory footprint rather than multi-threaded compute or local disk IOPS. The configuration is matched to in-memory caching layers, relational databases requiring substantial buffer pools, search indexing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.

It includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached volumes, and features a baseline network throughput of 7 Gbps. Performance evaluations highlight top-quartile single-core CPU execution and solid text processing capabilities, though multi-threaded scores and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth remain modest. The substantial memory footprint and dedicated compute allocation make this instance well suited for memory-intensive workloads including Redis cache layers, intermediate-scale relational databases, and enterprise applications requiring high memory density.
